items.title: Airbag control module software
items.summary: The occupant restraint controller could have software that disables the driver, passenger and knee airbags without warning.

items.title: Second-row center-seat recliner strap
items.summary: The strap can bind on the trim so the seat back doesn't lock upright (FMVSS 207).

items.title: B-pillar trim and curtain airbag
items.summary: Upper B-pillar trim may not be fully seated and could interfere with side-curtain airbag deployment.

items.title: Rear camera (CVPAM software)
items.summary: Park-assist module software may stop the rearview image displaying in reverse.

items.title: Third-row seat belt buckles
items.summary: Third-row occupants may not be able to reach or fasten the buckle.

items.title: Steering column control module weld
items.summary: A poorly welded clockspring/column module can stop the driver's airbag deploying. Part of a multi-model Stellantis campaign.

items.title: Rear camera (radio software)
items.summary: Radio software may prevent the rearview image from displaying.

items.title: Rear camera module software
items.summary: Incorrect camera-module software may stop the rearview image displaying.

items.title: Door trim may detach
items.summary: Driver and passenger door trim may not have been installed properly and can come off on the road.

items.title: Window quarter trim may detach
items.summary: Quarter trim on the door windows may not be secured and can come off.

items.title: Camera harness (2026 Grand Wagoneer)
items.summary: The front camera harness may not be connected, which can blank the rearview image.

items.title: Gear-position indicator software
items.summary: The gear selection indicator may not display, which risks a rollaway.

items.title: ESC and brake-assist software (2026)
items.summary: Brake control module software may cause a loss of stability control and electronic brake assist.

items.title: Rear camera image (2026, multi-model)
items.summary: The rearview image may fail to display in reverse.

items.title: Tire pressure monitoring software
items.summary: TPMS may fail to detect low pressure or light the warning lamp.

items.title: Roof rack crossbar pivot bolts
items.summary: Pivot bolts may not have been tightened, so the crossbars can detach.

tsbs.title: Air suspension inoperable (early 2022 builds)
tsbs.summary: For 2022 WS trucks with Quadra-Lift (sales code SER) built on or before Feb 15, 2022: check for unseated air lines, unplugged ASCM or height sensors, and shipping caps left on the vent hose. DTC C15AE-00.

tsbs.title: Blank or unresponsive 10.1 in / 12 in center display
tsbs.summary: Radio (R1 head unit) software update to perform before replacing the display.

tsbs.title: Electric power steering module update
tsbs.summary: EPS module flash for MIL or EPS warning messages.

tsbs.title: Telematics box module update
tsbs.summary: TBM reflash for inoperative remote functions or Wi-Fi.

tsbs.title: NHTSA investigation: engine stall with intermittent restart
tsbs.summary: Opened in 2024 into 2022 Ram 1500 and Wagoneer engines shutting off at low speed.

timeline.change: Sergio Marchionne announces the Grand Wagoneer name will return (Detroit auto show, January)
Grand Wagoneer Concept shown September 3 with no Jeep badging
Launch model year (revealed March 11, 2021): Wagoneer 5.7 eTorque (392 hp) and Grand Wagoneer 6.4 (471 hp). Early builds hit by air-suspension TSB 02-001-22 and several software recalls
Wagoneer L and Grand Wagoneer L (130 in wheelbase) debut with the 3.0 Hurricane twin-turbo six: 420 hp, or 510 hp high-output in Grand Wagoneers
Hemi V8s dropped, all trucks Hurricane-powered. February: Jeep says Wagoneer will stop being a sub-brand. IIHS 2024 Top Safety Pick (Wagoneer)
High-output Hurricane rises to 540 hp and 521 lb-ft. Last year of the standalone Wagoneer nameplate
Facelift revealed October 14, 2025: every truck is a Grand Wagoneer, Jeep badges, no chrome, new trims including the short-wheelbase Upland. Standard-output 420-hp Hurricane only. Starts at $64,740

identify.intro: Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer, their L versions and three engines all share one body, and the badges changed in 2026. Here's how to tell what you're looking at.

items.head: Wagoneer vs Grand Wagoneer (2022–2025)
items.body: Same body and size. Grand Wagoneers have a two-tone black roof, fender flares, power retractable side steps, a 12.3-inch cluster and a different grille, and air suspension is standard. Wagoneers have a standard side step and a 10.25-inch cluster, and air suspension was optional. From 2026 everything is badged Grand Wagoneer, with Jeep logos front and rear.

items.head: Short vs L
items.body: L models ride on a 130.0-inch wheelbase (123.0 standard) and are 226.7 inches long (214.7 standard). Look for a longer rear door-to-D-pillar section and quarter glass.

items.head: Which engine
items.body: AMSOIL's lookups list engine code T for the 5.7 Hemi (sales code EZL), J for the 6.4 Hemi (ESG) and P for the 3.0 Hurricane, split into EFH (standard output) and EFC (high output). The window sticker or a VIN decoder confirms which one you have, and that decides the oil grade.

items.head: Air or coil suspension
items.body: Quadra-Lift trucks carry sales code SER, show ride-height controls next to the Selec-Terrain toggle and offer Tire Jack mode in the Suspension menu. Coil trucks can't be raised from the cabin.

items.head: 4x4 system and off-road package
items.body: Quadra-Trac I has no low range. Two-speed trucks (Quadra-Trac II, Quadra-Drive II) have a low-range selection. The Advanced All-Terrain Group adds 18-inch all-terrain tires, front tow hooks, skid plates, a 3.92 axle and the rear electronic LSD, so check under the front for the skid plate.
